extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent applicants/practitioners in the Republic of Korea
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and examination criteria for drafting the description, background, embodiments, industrial applicability, and claims of a Korean patent application and for examiners to assess compliance with the Patent Act and Enforcement Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement requirement / Practicability
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention related to the claims must be able to be practiced with the embodiments disclosed in the description; if a certain embodiment for practicing the invention related to the claims is deemed different from the embodiment disclosed in the description, the examiner shall notify a ground for rejection citing violation of Article 42(3)(i) of the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When notifying enablement violations, specify the corresponding claims. If the description pursuant to Article 21(3) is present but not clear/detailed enough for the claimed invention to be practiced, notify under Article 42(3). For applications filed after Jan 1, 2015, propose amendment under Article 46 rather than immediate invalidation; for earlier applications, different consequences may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of description / disclose technical implication
rubrics_metrics.description: The description must disclose the invention so that a person skilled in the art can understand the technical implication of the invention given the skill level at filing, including what unresolved tasks exist in the technical field and how those tasks are solved and with which means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This disclosure clarifies the technical matter and scope sought for protection so third parties can understand the invention from the specification alone. The general method (problem → solution → means → effects) is the internationally adopted practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required/typical sections of the description
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle the description should contain: Title of the Invention, Technical Field, Background Art, Prior Art Literature, Brief Description of the Drawing(s), Summary of Invention, Detailed Description for Practicing Invention, Industrial Applicability, Consignment Number, and Sequence Listing Free Text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each section should be clear and precise enough for a skilled person to understand and reproduce the invention. Sections need not be separately prepared if their contents are understandable from the overall description. Where some sections cannot be filled (e.g., invention discovered by chance), omission may be acceptable if the invention can be understood without them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Field statement
rubrics_metrics.description: State the technical field clearly and briefly; related technical fields may be disclosed too. At least one technical field should be indicated unless a skilled person can identify it without explicit description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may refer to the International Patent Classification (IPC) when known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of Invention components
rubrics_metrics.description: The summary should include the technical problems to be solved, the means for solving those problems, and the effects of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For technical problems: state the prior art issue that is the objective. For means: state the type of means used; may be omitted if a skilled person can understand from other parts of the specification. For effects: state particular effects (especially superiority over prior art) as they may be recognized to confirm inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed description for practicing the invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide at least one detailed description for practicing the invention, preferably in various ways, so that a person skilled in the art can figure out how to practice the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State technical means (not merely functions). Where multiple technical means exist, explain inter-relationships producing effects. Include functions and configuration; for some fields (e.g., computers) explaining functions and connections can be more appropriate than detailed hardware. Provide many embodiments when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embodiment disclosure requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When claims are written generically, state representative embodiments corresponding to the generic description, unless a skilled person can derive details from the generic description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include basic data, comparative embodiments (technically closest to the invention), and alternative embodiments; specify differences between embodiments and show reference numbers for drawings in parentheses after technical terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of grounds for numerical limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: For numerical limitations applied to technical means, disclose the ground for the limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If experiment data are used, describe test methods, measurement tools, and test conditions in detail so a skilled person can reproduce results. If materials/devices that are hard to obtain are used, disclose manufacturing processes or sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of standard/recognized terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Use standard terms or academic terms generally recognized in the technical field; use chemical symbols, mathematical symbols and molecular formulas widely used in the technical field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When drawings are present, describe them in the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Where industrial applicability is hard to determine, state the utilization method, industrial applicability, or manufacturing method in the Industrial Applicability section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If industrial applicability can be well inferred from other parts of the specification, additional description may not be necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background art disclosure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Background art refers to conventional art beneficial for understanding the invention and conducting prior art searches and examination; it shall be disclosed in the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed after July 1, 2011, failure to disclose related background art is a ground for rejection under Article 42(3)(ii). The background art should be related to the invention defined by the claim limitations, considering technical field, problems, solutions, and effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art literature citation details
rubrics_metrics.description: When possible, disclose information on prior art literature: for patent literature include country of publication, gazette name, publication number, publication date; for non-patent literature include author, title, publisher, date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the cited literature itself describes proper background art, mere citation of that literature may suffice. Where multiple prior art documents exist, disclose the literature(s) closest to the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative disclosure when no background art exists
rubrics_metrics.description: If no background art can be assumed because the invention is based on novel ideas totally different from existing technology, replace background art with disclosure of existing technology in the closest technical field or describe the difficulty in finding proper background art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exception recognizes pioneering or highly novel inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegitimate background art: omission
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Background Art section and the whole description only disclose the technical problem, solution and effects but no background art, it may be deemed illegitimate and subject to rejection under Article 42(3)(ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may notify a ground for rejection in such cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegitimate background art: unrelated background material
rubrics_metrics.description: Background art that is not related to the invention for which protection is sought (considering technical field, technical problems, solutions, effects) is illegitimate; examples include background art about unrelated product features or background art only applicable to subject matter disclosed in the description but not in the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also applies where a divisional application's background art is not related to the divisional claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illegitimate background art: mere basic technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure that only describes basic/general technology of the technical field may not be deemed sufficient background art if it is not beneficial in understanding the invention or in conducting prior art searches and examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether such basic-technology disclosure suffices depends on whether proper background art is well known or easily obtained; examiners may suggest prior art literature when they know appropriate documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner notification for illegitimate background art
rubrics_metrics.description: When background art disclosure is illegitimate, the examiner shall notify a ground for rejection under Article 42(3)(ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination should consider the current status of the technical field, accumulation of existing technology, and applicant/inventor R&D activities. The requirement may be a ground for rejection but not necessarily for certain other procedures (e.g., Article 63-2 disclosure or invalidation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant response to background-art rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon notice of rejection for failure to describe background art, the applicant should amend by adding information on prior art literature in the Background Art or Prior Art Literature sections, and supply a written argument indicating that the background art is disclosed in the cited literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no proper background art exists, the applicant may respond with a written argument explaining that the invention is based on novel ideas and no proper background art can be found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling foreign-language portions and translation errors
rubrics_metrics.description: If parts of the specification are written in a foreign language making the description unclear, the examiner shall give the applicant an opportunity to explain and may return the application; if the unread part is not needed for understanding, do not return but order amendment citing Article 46. Translation errors alone should not by themselves lead to rejection unless they result in failure to meet description requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious: amendment after translation errors may add new matter or change the invention; examiner should examine thoroughly to avoid adding undisclosed technical matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inconsistency or ambiguity in technical terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Where different technical terms are used across the description and claims making the invention difficult to practice, notify rejection under Article 42(3). Where terms in the description and claims do not clearly match or are ambiguous, notify rejection under Article 42(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Undefined or unclear academic/technical terms, or lack of original-language/Chinese-character equivalents when needed, can be ground for rejection under Article 42(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark and product name usage in specification
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle, stating a trademark or product name is not allowed in a specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptionally allowed when the product can be easily obtained and its inclusion is unlikely to change the invention's content (quality/composition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification method and specificity of rejection grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: When notifying rejection for enablement or description-method violations, the examiner shall specify any violation and the corresponding claims (especially for enablement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the description method requirement (Article 21(3)) is violated but the claims can still be practiced, the description may still be considered legitimate. Distinct procedures apply depending on filing date (pre-2015 vs post-2015) regarding amendment proposals under Article 46.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and numbering of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims shall include at least one claim to be protected; claims must be supported by the description and set forth the invention clearly and concisely (Article 42(4)). Claims may include independent and dependent claims; the number of claims should be reasonable relative to the nature of the invention. Each claim must be entered on a new line and numbered in Arabic numerals in order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A claim that refers to another claim must state the number referred to; multiple dependent claims have specific restrictions (cannot serve as basis for other multiple dependent claims). The claim from which another depends should precede it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of invention/scope determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention for which protection is sought is determined by the limitations recited in each claim in accordance with the applicant’s will; the description/drawings are considered only when claims are indefinite or technical term meanings are ambiguous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not determine protection scope based on the description beyond claim limitations; abstracts cannot be used to decide protection scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must be supported by the description (support requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner determines support by whether a person skilled in the art can figure out that subject matters corresponding to the claim limitations are disclosed in the description; support is judged by whether claims depart from the scope grasped by a skilled person based on the description, not by literal identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cases lacking support include: (i) claim limitations (e.g., numeric) not disclosed or implied in the description; (ii) claim terms different from description rendering correspondence ambiguous; (iii) claims recite means/steps for functions but no specific configuration is disclosed; (iv) description cannot be extended/generalized to the claimed scope by a skilled person (e.g., claims defined only by technical effects while description shows only specific means). Examiners should consider the level of skill in the art.
